Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short proposal that aims to do two things: 1) make Redwood’s per-token economics competitive with the cloud endpoints you’re evaluating, and 2) provide a clear, low-friction path to switch production traffic without a long-term heavy lift. Key points below; attached is a one-page commit ladder for your legal and procurement teams.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Commitment ladder (12 months):
  - Tier 1: 0–500M tokens / month => $0.0065 per token (baseline)
  - Tier 2: 500M–2B tokens / month => $0.0048 per token
  - Tier 3: >2B tokens / month => $0.0039 per token
- Transitory credits: To de-risk switching, we’ll provide $150K in onboarding credits one-time, usable over first 90 days (applies to hosting and token usage).
- Short-term trial SLA: 45-day pilot with 99.5% uptime target on Dedicated-backed routes; automatic fallback to hosted multitenant model if we need to scale quickly.
- Technical support: Dedicated SE time during migration window + 24/7 on-call for the first 7 days after cutoff.

Why this is competitive: from the benchmark you shared, OpenAI’s conversational pricing for similar models is around $0.006–$0.007/token for higher-latency endpoints; Anthropic’s higher-capacity offerings come in slightly higher when you consider throughput needs and networking egress. Our ladder is designed to undercut those numbers at scale while preserving predictable latency and cache-efficiencies that matter for your real-time use cases.

Next asks: can you confirm the procurement contact we should send the formal MSA to? Also, which model variants (gpt-ish vs long-context) are you evaluating so we can finalize kernel/quantization guidance in the technical annex?

Attaching: 20261125-nova-commit-proposal.pdf (commit table + basic SLA)

Best,

Ben / Lauren —

Forwarding Emma’s procurement questions. Quick thoughts below before I reply:

- Egress: our per-token price is fully-burdened for hosted inference (includes network egress within standard regions); if they need special cross-region egress or dedicated private peering beyond standard limits, that’s an add-on. Say that explicitly.
- Credits: recommend we make the $150K credits usable over 120 days (extend from 90) but with a clause that unused credits expire — that reduces objections about ramp timing.
- MSA + SOC2: send a redline, but do not promise custom retention beyond our standard 13-month audit logs unless they pay for extended retention add-on.
- Competitive angle: Emma’s note makes clear they’re benchmarking OpenAI/Anthropic. If they push for a side-by-side rebate, offer a 60-day price-protection clause which lets them convert committed spend to a matched rate if a competing provider posts a lower public list at the time of invoice. This is limited, non-transferrable, and requires proof (invoice).

Draft reply plan: confirm egress scope, extend credits to 120 days, attach MSA redlines (condense to the common fields), and offer the 60-day price-protection addendum. Also include a short technical appendix listing model variants and recommended quantization so they know the latency tradeoffs.

Can you draft the MSA redline? Ben, can you run the price-protection wording by legal? I’ll assemble the appendix.

— Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Hart <emma@ava-systems.com>, contracts@ava-systems.com

Emma / Bridget —

Thanks for the questions — answering inline and attaching a short MSA redline and technical appendix.

1) Egress / fully-burdened price: the per-token rates in the ladder are inclusive of standard regional network egress for hosted API calls. Cross-region egress (data transferred between regions or out to non-standard destinations) is charged separately; we’ve called that out in the appendix.

2) Credits window: we can extend the onboarding credits to be usable over 120 days (one-time $150K credit). Unused credits expire after day 120; credits apply to usage and hosting only (not professional services).

3) MSA / SOC2: attached is a redline that reflects standard 13-month audit log retention and SOC2 attestations. For extended retention (24+ months) or custom KMS/HSM integrations, we’d need an add-on.

4) Price-protection addendum: we can offer a limited 60-day price-protection clause. If Ava provides verifiable, public proof of a lower per-token list price from a named competitor for a functionally equivalent offering, we’ll match that list price for the next invoice period on committed tokens up to the committed volume. This is subject to legal approval and requires a written claim from procurement.

5) Migration support: committed SE hours and 24/7 on-call for the 7-day immediate cutover period will be included. We’ll coordinate the exact runbook after LOI.

Attachments: 20261125-nova-commit-proposal.pdf, ava-sla-redlines.docx, technical-appendix-nova.pdf

Next steps: if this looks OK I’ll send the formal LOI and DocuSign link. Bridget — can you confirm whether your legal needs a redline meeting this week?
